verses.text: Zedekiah son of Josiah became king of Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made him king of the land of Judah.
But neither he, nor his officials, nor the people of the land listened to the words the LORD spoke through the prophet Jeremiah.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to the prophet Jeremiah with this request: "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."
At this time Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, because he had not yet been put in prison.
Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt. When the Babylonians who were surrounding Jerusalem heard the news, they pulled back from Jerusalem.
Then the LORD's message came to the prophet Jeremiah:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to ask me, 'Look, Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, will go back to its own land, Egypt.
Then the Babylonians will come back and attack this city. They will capture it and burn it down.'
This is what the LORD says: Do not fool yourselves by thinking, 'The Babylonians will surely leave us.' They will not leave.
Even if you defeated the whole Babylonian army attacking you, and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would get up and burn this city down."
After the Babylonian army had pulled back from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to claim his share of property among the people there.
But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard there, Irijah son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, arrested the prophet Jeremiah and said, "You are deserting to the Babylonians!"
Jeremiah said, "That is not true! I am not deserting to the Babylonians." But Irijah would not listen. He arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were furious with Jeremiah. They beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had turned into a prison.
Jeremiah was put into a cell in an underground dungeon, and he stayed there a long time.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he asked him privately, "Is there any message from the LORD?" Jeremiah answered, "Yes, there is. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What crime have I committed against you, your officials, or these people that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not attack you or this land'?
Now please listen, my lord the king. Please let me bring my request to you. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."

So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the courtyard of the guard. Every day he was given a loaf of bread from the street of the bakers, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.
